title: Collect triage feedback from replies to the bot's comments

thread.author: daniel-keenan
thread.body:
Every triage comment asks the reader to change the label if a rating looks wrong, and to reply saying why. The label change fixes that issue; **the reply is the only input that can fix a rule**. Nothing collects those replies today.

Child of gitlab-org/gitlab-runner#39676.

## Why replies, and not label changes

A label change on its own is ambiguous — it could mean the rule was misapplied, the rule itself is wrong, the person disagrees with the rule, or they know something the bot cannot see. Only the first two are actionable, and nothing distinguishes them without a reason attached.

Label changes still matter, but as a pointer to **where** disagreement concentrates, not as evidence the bot was wrong. Many corrections at one severity boundary is a rubric problem; scattered single-rung tweaks are noise, and chasing them would create churn.

## Mechanism

Each step below was verified against the live project before being written down.

**Finding the issues.** A project notes search for the comment marker returns every issue the bot has commented on — 66 distinct issues from one page. The bot's own comment is the index, so there is no list to maintain and nothing to lose when a CI artifact expires.

**Identifying feedback.** Only replies in the same discussion thread as the bot's comment count. GitLab attaches a **Reply** to the original note and converts it into a thread, so this works on the comments already posted and needs no change to how the bot writes them. A new top-level comment is not collected — which is why the ask must be "reply to the bot", not "comment on the issue".

**Not reporting the same reply twice.** The bot adds an emoji reaction to a reply once it has been collected, and skips reacted replies on later runs. The marker lives on the issue, so it survives regardless of CI state, and the reporter can see their feedback was picked up. Only the bot's own reaction counts — a teammate reacting must not silently mark feedback as collected — and anything ambiguous counts as not collected, since re-reporting is noise while dropping feedback loses it for good.

**Bounding the work.** Intersect with issues updated in the last 10 days. A reply bumps `updated_at`, so only recently-updated issues can carry new feedback. This is a fetch filter, not the deduplication mechanism.

**Cadence.** A weekly pipeline schedule, separate from the nightly triage run: different job, different audience, different artifact.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A command collects replies to the bot's triage comments and reports them
- [ ] Only thread replies are treated as feedback; top-level comments are not
- [ ] A reply is reported once — acknowledged with a reaction from the bot's own account, and skipped thereafter
- [ ] A reaction from anyone other than the bot does not mark a reply as collected
- [ ] Label changes are reported alongside, as a count per severity and priority boundary rather than as a correctness verdict
- [ ] It runs on its own weekly schedule and writes a report artifact
- [ ] It is read-only apart from the acknowledgement reaction

## Out of scope

- Treating human labels as ground truth. The team's historical `severity::2` rate of about 9% turned out to sit below what the documented ladder gives, so tuning toward human labels would have tuned away from the handbook.
- Reading issue comments as an input to triage itself. Related and useful, but a different change — tracked in gitlab-org/gitlab-runner#39676.

thread.author: cam_swords
thread.body:
- **Flag** and current category — [`FF_DISABLE_UMASK_FOR_DOCKER_EXECUTOR`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/blob/main/helpers/featureflags/flags.go#L15), default `false`. Epic category: **Off by default — needs a decision** (reclassified from *Permanent configuration*, because #37304 asks to switch it on by default).
- **Introduced by** — !2539 ("Replace umask usage with files permission change when a non-root image used"), @tmaczukin, v13.7.0 (merged 2020-12-01). Part of #1736 (closed), which set out to remove `umask 0000` from the Docker executor.
- **Flip history** — The default has never changed. It has been `false` since 2020-11-30, so 5.8 years. What the flag does changed on 2026-09-29 (2f3d08e6b, "Docker: Change ownership of the full builds directory when not shared"): it now chowns the whole builds directory when that directory isn't on a shared volume, and only the checkout and temp files when it is.
- **Open issues** referencing the flag
  - #37304: Enable FF_DISABLE_UMASK_FOR_DOCKER_EXECUTOR by default (~customer ~"priority::2", Backlog). Lists #30949 as a possible blocker.
  - #30949: More than 1024 characters of stderr from the image causes a runner system failure when the flag is on. Possibly fixed by 6d59cb2a2 / ca98a3c9a (2021, overflow and stderr uid/gid parsing tests). Needs checking.
  - #29330: A container user set explicitly isn't detected, because the runner inspects the image rather than the container.
  - #39840: Concrete path, directories created below `CI_BUILDS_DIR` are private to the image user. This is the same umask/ownership question on the `FF_CONCRETE` path, and it bears on whether the legacy `umask 0000` behaviour needs to survive.
- **Author contacted?** — Not yet.
- **Verdict** — **Keep for now, decision deferred.** The flag stays as it is: not removed, and not elevated to configuration. The concrete implementation (`FF_CONCRETE`) doesn't apply `umask 0000` at all. It already behaves as if this flag defaulted to on, so for now the concrete path doesn't need the flag. We expect that behaviour to break (#39840 is an early sign), and the umask-or-ownership handling will probably need to come back to the concrete path. Deciding this flag's future before then would be premature, so the decision waits until the concrete path's permission handling settles.
- **Action** — No MR. The flag and the legacy code path stay unchanged. Revisit once the concrete path's handling of umask and ownership is settled, for example when #39840 is resolved or if umask handling has to be added back to the concrete path.

## Related

It's likely https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/work_items/39540+ requires the same decision as this feature flag.

title: Service health check dials only the last address of a service, failing for IPv4-only services on dual-stack networks

thread.author: davux
thread.body:
## Summary

On the default network, the service health-check container is given only the **last** address of the service, so on a network with IPv6 enabled it always dials the service over IPv6. A service listening on IPv4 only then fails the health check although it's up.

## Details

`createHostConfigForServiceHealthCheck` (`executors/docker/docker.go`) builds the health-check container's `ExtraHosts` in a loop that reassigns the slice on each iteration:

```go
for _, ip := range service.IP {
    extraHosts = []string{service.ID[:min(12, len(service.ID))] + ":" + ip}
}
```

`getContainerIPAndExposedPorts` appends the IPv4 address before the global IPv6 one, so only the IPv6 entry survives. The build container, by contrast, gets every address (`executors/docker/services.go`, `for _, ip := range linkee.IP`).

`gitlab-runner-helper health-check` retries silently on dial errors, so the job log only shows repeated `dialing <short-id>:<port>...` lines until the timeout, then `*** WARNING: Service ... probably didn't start properly.`

## Reproduction

GitLab.com SaaS runner (`gitlab-runner 19.5.0~pre.2159.ga8432a3e`, `saas-linux-small-amd64`), service `typedb/typedb:3.13.6`, which listens on `0.0.0.0` only:

```yaml
probe:
  image: node:26-alpine
  services:
    - name: typedb/typedb:3.13.6
      alias: typedb
  script:
    - cat /etc/hosts
    - for a in $(awk '/[[:space:]]typedb([[:space:]]|$)/ {print $1}' /etc/hosts); do nc -z -w 3 "$a" 8000 && echo "$a open" || echo "$a refused"; done
```

The service gets both `172.17.0.3` and `fd76:5338:4685:1:0:242:ac11:3`; `172.17.0.3:8000` accepts connections, `[fd76:5338:4685:1:0:242:ac11:3]:8000` refuses them, and the health check times out after 30 seconds dialing the service's short ID.

## Likely cause

349f97b01 (Add IPv6 address when emulating links functionality), on top of e69da0345 (Emulate deprecated Docker links functionality with ExtraHosts).

## Suggested fix

Append each address to `extraHosts` instead of reassigning it. Logging dial errors in `health-check` would also make this kind of failure much easier to diagnose.

title: Runner tokens with an instance prefix are not recognized

thread.author: nwittstruck
thread.body:
## Summary

GitLab can add an [optional instance prefix](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/388379) in front of runner and CI job tokens (admin setting `instance_token_prefix`, behind feature flag `custom_prefix_for_all_token_types`, disabled by default). With prefix `acme`, a runner token looks like `acme-glrt-...` instead of `glrt-...`.

GitLab Runner does not expect this. Two places only look at the very start of the token, and both break once a prefix is added:

- `network.TokenIsCreatedRunnerToken` in `network/gitlab.go` checks for `glrt-`. It decides whether `unregister` removes one runner manager or deletes the whole runner.
- `helpers.ShortenToken` in `helpers/shorten_token.go` strips `glrt-`/`glcbt-`. It builds the short token used all over the runner.

With a prefix in use, `unregister` deletes the entire runner instead of just one manager, and every runner on the instance gets the same short token, so different runners share caches and build directories.

* Parent issue: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/388379
* Rollout issue: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/522940

## Steps to reproduce

Reproduced on a GDK:

1. In the Rails console, enable the flag and set the prefix:
```ruby
Feature.enable(:custom_prefix_for_all_token_types)
ApplicationSetting.current.update!(instance_token_prefix: 'acme')
```
2. Create two instance runners in GitLab (Admin area > CI/CD > Runners > New instance runner). Their tokens should start with `acme-glrt-`.
3. Register runner 1 on two hosts. You can simulate this with two config directories, each with its own `.runner_system_id`, and runner 2 on a third host:
   `gitlab-runner register --non-interactive --config host-a/config.toml --url http://gdk.test:3000 --token acme-glrt-... --executor shell --name host-a` (same command for host-b with runner 1's token, and host-c with runner 2's token).
4. Look at the `runner=` field in the output: it is `acme-glrt` for all three hosts, although host-a/host-b and host-c belong to different runners.
5.  To unregister, run `gitlab-runner unregister --config host-a/config.toml --all-runners`.
6. Runner 1 no longer exists in the GitLab UI, so host-b lost its runner too, although only host-a unregistered.

## Actual behavior

- `unregister` on one host deletes the whole runner (`DELETE /api/v4/runners`), removing it for every other host sharing that runner. 
- `register --token acme-glrt-...` takes the legacy "verify existing token" path: it logs "Token specified trying to verify runner...", "If you want to register use the '-r' instead of '-t'.", and "is alive" instead of "is valid", and writes `id = 0` and no `token_obtained_at` to `config.toml`.
- Every runner on the instance gets the same short token, `acme-glrt`, since `ShortenToken` strips not correctly. This short token is used in a few places, so different runners can collide. docker+machine runners on the same host with the same `MachineName` template can adopt or remove each other's machines.

## Expected behavior

Tokens with an instance prefix should be handled the same as plain `glrt-` tokens: `unregister` should remove only that host's runner manager, `register` should use the normal path and log "is valid", and the short token should be taken from the token body, distinct per runner. 

## Relevant logs and/or screenshots

<details><summary> register / unregister output </summary>

```sh
# register (host-a)
Runtime platform                                    arch=arm64 os=linux pid=19710 revision=eba7e9d6 version=v1.11.1-0.20260928083038-eba7e9d6eaa0
Token specified trying to verify runner...
WARNING: If you want to register use the '-r' instead of '-t'.
Verifying runner... is alive                        correlation_id=... runner=acme-glrt runner_name=host-a
Runner registered successfully. Feel free to start it, but if it's running already the config should be automatically reloaded!

# register (host-c, a different runner, same short token)
Token specified trying to verify runner...
Verifying runner... is alive                        correlation_id=... runner=acme-glrt runner_name=host-c

# unregister (host-a)
WARNING: Unregistering all runners
Unregistering runner from GitLab succeeded          correlation_id=... runner=acme-glrt runner_name=host-a
```

</details>

## Environment description
Reproduced on GDK, with the `custom_prefix_for_all_token_types` feature flag enabled and `instance_token_prefix` set to `acme`. 

### Used GitLab Runner version

```
Version:      v1.11.1-0.20260928083038-eba7e9d6eaa0
Git revision: eba7e9d6
Git branch:   HEAD
GO version:   go1.27.1
Built:        2026-09-28T08:30:38Z
OS/Arch:      linux/arm64
```

## Possible fixes

Allow an optional alphanumeric instance prefix followed by a hyphen before `glrt-` and `glcbt-` in both `TokenIsCreatedRunnerToken` (`network/gitlab.go`) and `ShortenToken` (`helpers/shorten_token.go`), for example with a shared pattern `([A-Za-z0-9]+-)?`. `glrtr-` tokens (runners registered with a registration token) never get an instance prefix, so they stay as they are.

A runner release with this fix is needed before GitLab enables the feature flag; the GitLab docs should state the minimum runner version once a prefix is configured.
